column1: # What the installer CANNOT do for you, in the order you should do it.
# Everything not listed here is copied verbatim and needs no work. That is the
# point of the core/examples split: `core/` states the method with no stack token
# in it, so there is nothing in it to rewrite. This file is the residue.
# tier
#   author    not copied from the source at all -- you write it for this project.
#   retarget  copied, but it names commands or paths that belong to the source.
# This file drives ADAPTATION-TODO.md, so a row for a defect that no longer exists
# sends a human to fix something already fixed -- which teaches them to distrust the
# whole worklist. Five rows were dropped once the source stopped having the defect
# (the three command files, which now defer to meta/project-profile.md, and the two
# core/playbook/ files, whose /course/ links are gone). Before adding a row back,
# grep the install source for the defect. Before adding a new one, check it is real
# there too.
# The two retarget rows are gone as well: the source project's course framing was
# stripped out of orchestration/README.md and commands/README.md once the fork became
# the source of truth, so there is nothing left in the copied tree that names another
# project. What remains is the irreducible part -- the two files only you can write.
author
column3: NEW FILE. Does not exist upstream. The single source of truth for this project's facts: real gate commands, stack, layout, ports, DB. Every other file defers to it. RUN each command and `ls` each path before writing it down; mark anything unverified NEEDS CONFIRMATION.
